“Amid this progress and strong policy support, indicators of economic activity and employment have strengthened.” The statement’s pledge to let inflation run “moderately above 2 percent” for a time aligns with the average-inflation-targeting and makeup strategy outlined by Chair Powell at Jackson Hole (2020) and with modern New Keynesian guidance (Clarida, Galí, and Gertler) that anchoring expectations around target can enhance stabilization. Ongoing large-scale asset purchases and explicit forward guidance are consistent with the literature on QE and expectations management that eases financial conditions and supports credit intermediation. The small increases to IOER and the ON RRP rate are implementation tools of the floor system (Goodfriend, 2002), aimed at keeping money-market rates within the target range rather than signaling tightening. While the Committee remains data-dependent in a manner reminiscent of rule-based policy (Taylor principle), its outcome-based guidance and tolerance for a temporary overshoot indicate a dovish tilt relative to pre-2020 frameworks. Net tone: moderately positive for growth and financial conditions, with acknowledgement of residual risks from the virus.
